scenarios: a proposal is stored PROPOSED in the user layer, is UNTRUSTED with no tools, is refused on a call, and its process is never spawned
a definition that does not validate is refused, and a name a higher layer denied is refused at propose time
trusting a server whose credential the Core does not hold is refused; configuring the credential lets the trust succeed and only then does the server run
proposing needs task.author and trusting needs repository.trust; a sandbox guest holds neither
taking trust away returns the server to PROPOSED and stops the running program
the task that saw the proposal keeps seeing it untrusted; the next task sees the server ready
proof: the real Core with real configuration files and a real MCP server binary whose log file is the evidence that it was never started before it was trusted.
audit: ABSENT before: configuration reached the Core only from files and a boot environment variable; no propose, no trust transition, no run-time credential.
limitations: an agent proposes through a person's client rather than a tool (docs/17 defines the namespace as list/call/cancel); proposals live in the user layer only; the commands are not journaled — the configuration file is the durable record.
